description: Evaluation + classical models: metrics.py (AUROC, AUPRC, precision@k per drug, ECE + reliability table, bootstrap CIs resampling held-out DRUGS; scikit-learn + numpy only) and baselines.py (term-popularity prior; drug-similarity kNN using gene-set Jaccard now and structure Tanimoto when fingerprints exist; logistic regression; numpy matrix factorisation with documented negative sampling). Depends on FEAT-001 artifacts (reads research/kg/artifacts/*.parquet) and splits. Runs fully on the classical venv (no torch/RDKit needed).
steps: Read research/kg/.agents/plan.md and context.json FIRST, and read FEAT-001 findings for any artifact-schema notes.

Create research/kg/metrics.py (`[kg.metrics]` style, scikit-learn + numpy only): auroc(y_true,y_score); auprc(y_true,y_score); precision_at_k_per_drug(y_true_by_drug,y_score_by_drug,k) returning mean + per-drug series; expected_calibration_error(y_true,y_score,n_bins=10) returning (ece, reliability_table_df); bootstrap_ci(metric_fn, grouped_by_drug, n_boot=1000, seed=42, alpha=0.05) resampling held-out drugs with replacement and returning (point, lo, hi).

Create research/kg/baselines.py (`[kg.base]` style, scikit-learn + numpy only): term_popularity_prior(train_edges,n_terms); drug_similarity_knn(train_edges,drug_sim,k=25) where drug_sim is gene-set Jaccard from edges_drug_gene (and structure Tanimoto when feat_drug_structure exists); logistic_regression_baseline(features,train_edges,...); matrix_factorisation(train_edges,n_drugs,n_terms,dim=64,seed=42,neg_ratio=1) implemented in numpy with documented negative sampling from UNLABELED pairs (PU-aware); predict_scores(model,pairs). Reuse metrics.py for any internal scoring.
Document in a module docstring that absent (drug,term) pairs are UNLABELED (positive-unlabeled), not negatives, and that negatives for training are SAMPLED from the unlabeled set.

Create research/kg/tests/test_metrics.py: AUROC on a perfectly separable toy == 1.0; ECE of a perfectly-calibrated toy ~= 0; bootstrap_ci lo <= point <= hi. Create research/kg/tests/test_baselines.py: each baseline returns finite scores of the expected shape on a small synthetic graph built in the test. Provide __main__ assert-runners as a pytest fallback.
acceptance_criteria: metrics.bootstrap_ci resamples drugs (not pairs) and returns a point estimate bracketed by its CI.
Each of the four baselines produces finite scores of the correct shape when run against the FEAT-001 artifacts via a drug-wise split.
baselines.py docstring states the PU-learning (unlabeled != negative) caveat and the negative-sampling scheme.
verification: research/kg/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest research/kg/tests/test_metrics.py research/kg/tests/test_baselines.py  (fallback: run each tests/test_*.py directly with the venv python) — all pass
findings:
DONE & verified on the classical venv (sklearn + numpy only; no torch/RDKit). pytest: 10 passed (5 in test_metrics.py, 5 in test_baselines.py); the assert-based __main__ fallbacks in both test files also pass. Created research/kg/metrics.py, research/kg/baselines.py, research/kg/tests/test_metrics.py, research/kg/tests/test_baselines.py. Tests import the modules via sys.path.insert('..') so they run from any cwd and under both pytest and direct `python tests/test_*.py`.

metrics.py SIGNATURES (ablations/baselines/error_analysis call these):
- auroc(y_true, y_score) -> float. nan (printed note) if y_true single-class.
- auprc(y_true, y_score) -> float (average_precision_score). nan if no positives.
- precision_at_k_per_drug(y_true_by_drug, y_score_by_drug, k) -> (mean: float, per_drug: pd.Series). Accepts EITHER a dict {drug_id -> 1d array over that drug's candidate terms} OR 2d arrays shape (n_drugs, n_terms). per_drug is a pandas Series (name=f'precision_at_{k}') indexed by drug id; mean uses np.nanmean. k is clamped to available terms; ties broken by stable argsort.
- expected_calibration_error(y_true, y_score, n_bins=10) -> (ece: float, reliability_table: pd.DataFrame). Table has exactly n_bins rows, columns [bin_lo, bin_hi, count, mean_score, pos_rate, gap]; equal-width bins over [0,1]; ece is sample-weighted mean |mean_score - pos_rate|.
- bootstrap_ci(metric_fn, grouped_by_drug, n_boot=1000, seed=42, alpha=0.05) -> (point, lo, hi). RESAMPLES DRUGS (groups) with replacement, NOT pairs. `grouped_by_drug` is an ordered sequence of per-drug items; `metric_fn(list_of_items) -> scalar`. point = metric on full set; lo/hi = alpha/2 and 1-alpha/2 percentiles of the bootstrap stats (finite values only). Verified lo <= point <= hi.

baselines.py SIGNATURES + score array shapes (all finite, dispatched by predict_scores on model['kind']):
- term_popularity_prior(train_edges, n_terms) -> {kind:'term_popularity', term_prior: ndarray shape (n_terms,) in [0,1]}.
- gene_jaccard_similarity(drug_gene_edges, n_drugs) -> dense ndarray (n_drugs, n_drugs) symmetric Jaccard (helper to build drug_sim).
- drug_similarity_knn(train_edges, drug_sim, n_terms, k=25) -> {kind:'drug_knn', pos_by_drug, drug_sim, k, n_terms}. drug_sim is any (n_drugs,n_drugs) matrix -- gene_jaccard now, structure Tanimoto when feat_drug_structure exists (same shape, basis-agnostic). Score = similarity-weighted fraction of top-k training drugs that list the term, in [0,1].
- logistic_regression_baseline(features, train_edges, n_drugs, n_terms, neg_ratio=1, seed=42, C=1.0) -> {kind:'logreg', clf, features}. `features` is a callable (drug_index, term_index) -> 1d ndarray feature vector. Trains sklearn LogisticRegression on positives + PU pseudo-negatives.
- matrix_factorisation(train_edges, n_drugs, n_terms, dim=64, seed=42, neg_ratio=1, lr=0.05, reg=0.01, epochs=30) -> {kind:'mf', D: ndarray (n_drugs,dim), T: ndarray (n_terms,dim)}. numpy SGD, sigmoid(D[d].T[t]).
- sample_negatives(positives_set, n_drugs, n_terms, neg_ratio=1, seed=42) -> (m,2) int array of UNLABELED pairs (never overlaps positives). PU pseudo-negatives.
- predict_scores(model, pairs) -> 1d ndarray of finite scores aligned to `pairs` ((n,2) of (drug_index,term_index)). Dispatches on model['kind'] in {term_popularity, drug_knn, logreg, mf}. All four score ranges land in [0,1].

PU CAVEAT: baselines.py module docstring states absent (drug,term) pairs are UNLABELED (positive-unlabeled), not confirmed negatives, and that training negatives are SAMPLED from the unlabeled set (neg_ratio per positive, fixed seed) as pseudo-negatives, biasing scores optimistically. metrics.py docstring repeats that AUROC/AUPRC here treat unlabeled as pseudo-negative background (optimistic upper bounds). Fixed seed 42 throughout. Expects FEAT-001 artifact columns: edges_drug_term(drug_index,term_index,...), edges_drug_gene(drug_index,gene_index,...), nodes_drug/nodes_term indices.
